newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia to issue one-year bills less frequently.
newsitem.headline: Latvia to issue one-year bills less frequently.

text.p: The Latvian finance ministry said on Friday that it would start selling its 364-day Treasury bills once every eight weeks instead of once a week as at present.
The new system will start from December 4 and an average volume of 10 million lats to 15 million lats will be offered, the ministry said in a statement.
This replaces the current system where small volumes of 364-day T-bills were issued every week.
If the volume on offer is not sold immediately, it will be sold off during the following weeks, the ministry added.
Latvia currently holds one Treasury bill auction a week on a Wednesday and sells 28-day, 91-day, 182-day and 364-day paper.
The average yields were 9.95 percent, 10.34 percent, 11.75 percent and 12.52 percent respectively on these maturities at the last auction.
